fullstory.title: Rodgers, McCarthy and the Steelers

timeline.t: The Steelers announce Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for Friday's game against the Broncos, with Mason Rudolph set to start.
On The Pat McAfee Show, Rodgers says he will not return to Pittsburgh and accuses coach Mike McCarthy of dozing in meetings. He says he learned of the benching from tight end Pat Freiermuth.
The Steelers waive Rodgers, ESPN and NFL.com report. Past the trade deadline, any team can claim him; if none does he becomes an unrestricted free agent.
ESPN reports league sources say Rodgers' account was accurate. NFL Network reports sources say Rodgers wanted to take over play calling and McCarthy declined.
NFL Network and ESPN report the organization fully supports McCarthy. McCarthy tells reporters the benching was his decision and denies holding a grudge.

facts.c: Rodgers was inactive for Friday's game after a benching announced Tuesday night.

facts.s: Rodgers' claim. ESPN cites league sources saying his account was accurate

facts.c: Rodgers wanted play-calling control and McCarthy declined.
Benching was McCarthy's decision; he holds no grudge.

unknown: Whether any team claims Rodgers off waivers.
Whether the Steelers issue a formal statement. Neither ESPN nor NFL.com reported one.
Details from anonymous sources have not been confirmed on the record by the team.

updates.x: Story added to The Full Story from ESPN and NFL.com reporting. VAULT will mark changes here as sources update.

fullstory.title: TCU fires Sonny Dykes

timeline.t: No. 2 Utah beats TCU 38-17 in Fort Worth. TCU trails 17-0 at halftime, ties it at 17 with two Jeremy Payne touchdown runs and a field goal, then Utah scores 21 unanswered.
Dykes says his players battled hard after falling behind 17-0, credits Utah and praises quarterback Adam Schobel's first career start.
TCU fires Dykes the morning after the loss. The Horned Frogs are 5-6.
Sources tell ESPN Dykes is expected to be owed more than $20 million. Defensive coordinator Andy Avalos becomes interim coach.
Avalos says the team is working through a wave of emotions on a short week.
TCU plays at Texas Tech in the regular-season finale.

facts.c: TCU fired Sonny Dykes after the Utah loss.
Dykes is expected to be owed more than $20 million.
Dykes went 41-23 over five seasons and led TCU to the 2023 CFP title game in his first year.

unknown: Who TCU hires as its next head coach.
The final buyout figure. The $20 million number comes from sources.

updates.x: Story added to The Full Story from ESPN, AP and SI reporting.

fullstory.title: Navajo Stirling's knockout of Jiri Prochazka

timeline.t: Stirling knocks out Prochazka with a right hook at 4:58 of Round 2 in the UFC Qatar main event in Doha.
Stirling moves to 12-0, 7-0 in the UFC. It is his fourth straight knockout in 2026.
Prochazka's loss is his second straight knockout defeat, a first in his career.
Stirling's path to the title runs through champion Carlos Ulberg, his City Kickboxing teammate.

facts.s: Confirmed by ESPN and Yahoo Sports

facts.c: Some outlets say two or three seconds remained when it ended.
facts.s: Consistent with a 4:58 stoppage in a 5:00 round

unknown: Whether the UFC books a title fight against his teammate.

updates.x: Story added to The Full Story from ESPN, Yahoo Sports and TNT Sports reporting.

fullstory.title: The CFP rankings shake-up

timeline.t: Georgia is No. 1 in the fourth College Football Playoff rankings for the third straight week.
Utah (11-0), the only unbeaten team in the FBS, is No. 2. Texas is No. 3, Notre Dame No. 4 and Tennessee No. 5.
Alabama falls from No. 3 to No. 6, UCLA from No. 4 to No. 9 after its first loss, and Indiana from No. 8 to No. 14.

facts.c: Georgia is No. 1 for the third straight week.
Utah is the only undefeated team left in the FBS.
facts.s: Confirmed by the CFP and NCAA.com

unknown: Final playoff seeding. One more set of rankings comes after the regular season.

updates.x: Story added to The Full Story from the CFP and NCAA.com.

exclusive.title: The Week in VAULT: Nov 19–25
exclusive.preview: Four stories carried the week: a quarterback waived, a coach fired, a knockout that changed a division, and a new No. 1 in college basketball.
body: Steelers: Pittsburgh waived Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday after he criticized coach Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show, ESPN and NFL.com report. ESPN says league sources back Rodgers' account. NFL Network says the organization supports McCarthy. All of the inside detail rests on anonymous sourcing.

TCU: Sonny Dykes was fired the morning after a 38-17 loss to No. 2 Utah. Utah's 17th straight win clinched a spot in the Big 12 title game. Georgia stayed No. 1 in the CFP rankings and Alabama fell from No. 3 to No. 6.

MMA: Navajo Stirling knocked out Jiri Prochazka at 4:58 of Round 2 at UFC Qatar to move to 12-0. The result leaves the light heavyweight division with a puzzle, because the champion, Carlos Ulberg, is Stirling's teammate.
NFL: San Francisco beat Minnesota 35-10 in Mexico City to reach 9-1, and Buffalo beat Miami to match the league's best record.
College basketball: Houston went to No. 1 in the AP poll after winning the Players Era 8 tournament, in a week when four of the previous top five teams lost.

VAULT take (opinion): The common thread was speed. Within about 24 hours of the Utah loss TCU had a new interim coach, and the Steelers moved on Rodgers within a day of the interview. Expect the next news cycle to be about who claims Rodgers and who TCU hires.

exclusive.title: VAULT Power Rankings: NFL by record
exclusive.preview: Two teams share the best record in the league, and they sit atop their conferences: San Francisco and Buffalo, both 9-1.
body: Method: teams are ordered by winning percentage from the standings snapshot below. Ties are left tied and listed alphabetically. This is a record-based ranking, not a prediction.
Four teams are 8-2: Chicago, Detroit, Kansas City and Denver. Detroit and Denver hold the second seeds in their conferences.
At the bottom, the Chargers, Dolphins and Titans are all 1-9.
VAULT take (opinion): The 49ers' 35-10 win over Minnesota is the cleanest evidence in the top tier this week, because it came against a team with a 7-3 record.

exclusive.title: VAULT Power Rankings: NBA by record
exclusive.preview: The Lakers and Spurs are both 15-3, tied for the best record in the league.
body: Method: teams are ordered by winning percentage from the standings snapshot below. Ties are left tied. Teams have played different numbers of games, so winning percentage is used.
Philadelphia is 14-4 and leads the East. Minnesota, Houston and Memphis are all 13-5.
At the bottom, Milwaukee is 2-16, Sacramento is 2-15 and Utah is 3-16.
VAULT take (opinion): The West holds the top two spots, which makes the Spurs-Lakers debate on our Debates page a real one.

exclusive.title: Why Houston is No. 1: four of the top five lost
exclusive.preview: Houston did not just win. It beat the previous No. 1 on its way to a tournament title, in a week when most of the top five lost.
body: What happened: Houston won three games in three days at the Players Era 8 tournament in Las Vegas. That included a semifinal win over then-No. 1 Florida and a win over Kansas.
The vote: Houston received 55 of 59 first-place votes in the AP poll. Virginia, at 7-0, is No. 2 and Florida fell to No. 3.

The losses: Illinois beat Duke 99-78 and moved to No. 4. Tennessee beat Michigan State 61-46 and jumped from 14th to ninth. Duke and Michigan State fell out of the top 10, and defending champion Michigan fell out of the poll.
VAULT take (opinion): No. 1 votes follow results in November, not brands. Houston and Virginia are unbeaten teams with real wins, and the poll rewarded that.
